stated_availability: Three concordant statements, all pointing to a single Zenodo research compendium (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252). (1) Methods, p.2: "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper is at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252 to enable re-use of materials and improve reproducibility and transparency (Marwick, 2017). All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018). The R code is released under the MIT license, the data as CC-0, and figures as CC-BY, to enable maximum re-use." (2) Fig. 2 caption, p.4: "Further details about the model specifications and diagnostics are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252." (3) Data availability statement, p.10: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252." Article DOI: 10.1016/j.jas.2025.106281 (J. Archaeol. Sci. 180, 2025, 106281); single author with ORCID iD displayed on the title page; article itself carries "© 2025 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved". Descriptive record only — no L1-L6 mapping performed (L-levels are assigned at reproduction time from actual retrieval attempts).

F1.evidence: Data carry a DOI-based persistent identifier: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (Data availability statement, p.10). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 is a globally unique, resolvable PID, not a bare URL or an 'available on request' statement.

F2.evidence: Deposit is in Zenodo, which the paper itself describes as "a non-profit generic research data repository hosted by CERN that accepts any file format and freely assigns all publicly available uploads a DOI to make the files easily and uniquely citable (Peters et al., 2017)" (p.7). Zenodo deposits emit structured DataCite metadata (creator, title, publisher, publication year, resource type, rights) as a platform property. Richness of the record itself could not be inspected (supplementary/repository files deliberately not supplied); scored on the evidenced fact of a DOI-issuing repository deposit.

F3.evidence: The Zenodo/DataCite metadata record for 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 embeds the DOI as its Identifier element, and the paper's own metadata (Data availability statement, p.10, and Methods, p.2) explicitly carries the data identifier, giving bidirectional article-to-deposit linkage via PID.

F4.evidence: Zenodo is named in the instrument as an exemplar searchable registry; deposits are indexed via DataCite/OpenAIRE. Evidence: "openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (p.10). Not a personal website or unindexed server.

A1.evidence: Retrievable by DOI resolution over HTTPS. A1 assessed against the full research dataset, not just a supplement: "All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium" (p.2). data_completeness coverage_category = "complete" (5/5 datasets Tier 0-2), so the completeness rule does not zero A1.

A1_1.evidence: Protocol is HTTPS via the DOI resolver to Zenodo — open, free, universally implementable, no login, no subscription, no proprietary client. Data licensed CC-0: "the data as CC-0" (p.2).

A1_2.evidence: HTTPS/DOI resolution to Zenodo supports authentication and authorisation procedures where these are necessary (Zenodo offers restricted and embargoed deposits). No restriction is needed for this aggregate bibliometric and review-summary data, and none is imposed; the protocol nonetheless satisfies the 'where needed' condition.

A2.evidence: Zenodo is operated by CERN with a long-term preservation commitment and retains DOI/DataCite metadata (tombstone records) even if files are withdrawn. The paper endorses Zenodo precisely for this long-term availability property, contrasting it with GitHub, which "does not offer DOIs or the same commitments to long-term availability as Zenodo" (p.7).

I1.evidence: Data are deposited as part of an executable R research compendium (Marwick et al., 2018) from which "All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium" (p.2) — i.e. machine-parseable, R-readable structured files, not PDF tables or scanned images. Specific file formats are not enumerated in the article, so this is inferred from the evidenced compendium architecture rather than from an inspected file listing.

I2.evidence: No controlled vocabulary, ontology, thesaurus, or standardised term scheme is cited for the data. The five bibliometric variables (number of authors, number of pages, relative title length, Price index of reference recency, Shannon Index of reference diversity, pp.2-3) are described in prose with ad hoc naming; no PID-bearing vocabulary (e.g. Getty AAT, PeriodO, CIDOC-CRM) is referenced. Unscoreable/absent = 0.

I3.evidence: No evidence of typed/qualified relations from the dataset to other resources. The article cites the deposit DOI, but no relatedIdentifier assertions (e.g. 'isSupplementTo' the article DOI, 'isDerivedFrom' the Web of Science source) are documented in the paper, and the upstream Clarivate Web of Science / Journal Citation Indicator sources are cited by name only, without PIDs (p.2). Scores 0 as unevidenced.

R1.evidence: Data are described with a plurality of relevant attributes in Methods §2: source database, selection filters, sample sizes ("the Web of Science category 'Archaeology' and the Document type 'article' (n = 28,871)"), the retained sample ("I analysed 9697 papers published during 1975-2025", 20 journals), and definitions of every derived variable, following Fanelli and Glänzel (2013). Fig. 2 caption additionally points to the deposit for "further details about the model specifications and diagnostics".

R1_1.evidence: Explicit, machine-mappable licence: "The R code is released under the MIT license, the data as CC-0, and figures as CC-BY, to enable maximum re-use" (p.2). CC-0 maps to SPDX CC0-1.0 — an unambiguous public-domain dedication, not 'available on request'.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance of derivation: "This sample was collected from Clarivate's Web of Science database by first selecting the Web of Science category 'Archaeology' and the Document type 'article' (n = 28,871)... I then filtered the results to keep only articles published in the top-ranking 25 journals according to their h-indices as reported by Clarivate's Journal Citation Indicator. Finally, I excluded journals with less than 100 articles in the database, resulting in 20 journals" (p.2). Processing software identified (R Core Team, 2024) and model parameters specified (Fig. 2 caption: Zero-One Inflated Beta with logit link; Gaussian with identity link; Negative Binomial with log link).

R1_3.evidence: Meets domain-relevant community standards: the deposit is framed as a research compendium following the archaeological/computational community standard of Marwick et al. (2018) — "can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018)" (p.2) — deposited in a DataCite-compliant repository with explicit open licensing, the practice the paper itself codifies as the disciplinary norm (Fig. 6 checklist, p.9: "Project materials are openly available via DOI").

F1.evidence: Code carries a DOI: "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper is at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (p.2). This is an archival PID, not a GitHub URL — the paper explicitly rejects GitHub-only sharing because it "does not offer DOIs or the same commitments to long-term availability as Zenodo" (p.7).

F2.evidence: Code archived in Zenodo, which auto-generates structured DataCite metadata (creators, title, publisher, year, resource type, rights). The paper describes Zenodo as the repository that "freely assigns all publicly available uploads a DOI to make the files easily and uniquely citable" (p.7). Presence of CodeMeta.json / CITATION.cff could not be inspected (repository files deliberately not supplied); scored on the evidenced archival deposit.

F3.evidence: The DataCite record for 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 contains the DOI as its Identifier, and the article text carries the same identifier in both the Methods (p.2) and the Data availability statement (p.10), so metadata and artefact are explicitly linked by PID.

F4.evidence: Zenodo deposit is indexed in a searchable registry (DataCite/OpenAIRE), unlike an unarchived code host. The paper's Fig. 5C notes Zenodo as the most common deposit location among reviewed papers and endorses it over GitHub for exactly this reason (p.7).

A1.evidence: "The entire R code ... is at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (p.2) — retrievable by its identifier via DOI resolution over HTTPS; source code (R scripts), not compiled binaries, and stated to cover the whole analysis rather than a fragment.

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS/DOI to Zenodo: open, free, universally implementable, no authentication needed. The runtime is itself open-source and freely obtainable (R Core Team, 2024), so no proprietary licence stands between a reader and execution.

A1_2.evidence: The retrieval protocol (HTTPS via DOI resolver, Zenodo) supports authentication/authorisation procedures where required; no restriction is necessary for this code and none is applied — it is openly licensed under MIT.

A2.evidence: Zenodo/CERN retains DOI metadata independently of file availability (DataCite tombstone records). The paper selects Zenodo over GitHub precisely for "commitments to long-term availability" (p.7) and criticises journal supplementary files because they "are typically renamed and converted to different formats during the article production process" (p.7).

I1.evidence: Code is written in R, an open, standard, widely implemented language, and shared as script files in an executable compendium: "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper" (p.2). Not a proprietary or binary-only format.

I2.evidence: No software metadata vocabulary is evidenced — no CodeMeta.json, CITATION.cff, or other PID-bearing schema is mentioned in the article for this deposit. (The paper recommends such practices to others but does not state its own compendium's metadata files.) Unevidenced = 0.

I3.evidence: No qualified, PID-typed references from the code to its dependencies or related objects are evidenced. The paper recommends renv, Docker, and explicit dependency versioning to other authors ("the most robust and widely used include renv for R (Ushey and Wickham, 2025)", "authors should include a Dockerfile in the compendium", p.8) but does not state that its own compendium contains a lockfile, DESCRIPTION, or Dockerfile, nor does it list package version numbers in the article. Scores 0 as unevidenced.

R1.evidence: Code is documented in relation to the outputs it produces: "All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018)" (p.2), with the Fig. 2 caption directing readers to the deposit for "further details about the model specifications and diagnostics" — i.e. the artefact is described sufficiently for a reader to locate and run the analysis.

R1_1.evidence: "The R code is released under the MIT license" (p.2) — an explicit, standard, machine-mappable open-source licence (SPDX: MIT), distinct from the CC-0 applied to data and CC-BY to figures.

R1_2.evidence: Analytical provenance is documented: analysis environment identified (R Core Team, 2024); the derivation chain from Clarivate Web of Science through filtering to the 9697-paper sample is specified (p.2); and model parameters are given (Fig. 2 caption: "For recency of references a Zero-One Inflated Beta distribution family was used with a logit link function. For diversity of references and relative title length (ln) the Gaussian family was used with the canonical identity link function. For the number of authors pages the Negative Binomial family was used with a standard log link function"). Package-level version pinning is not stated in the article — a partial gap, but creation process, sources, and parameters are documented.

R1_3.evidence: Follows the research-compendium community standard for computational archaeology (Marwick et al., 2018), cited explicitly at the point of deposit (p.2), with archival DOI deposit and open licensing — the practices the paper's own Fig. 6 checklist (p.9) sets as the disciplinary standard ("Project materials are openly available via DOI"; "Simple, logical, fully self-contained project structure, ready to run").

barriers: paywall / subscription: the upstream sources for the principal dataset are Clarivate's Web of Science database and Journal Citation Indicator (p.2), both licensed products — re-collecting the raw records from source requires an institutional subscription (Tier 2), although the derived analysis data are stated to be deposited openly as CC-0 in Zenodo (Tier 0)

proprietary source terms: redistribution of bibliographic records extracted from a commercial index is constrained by the vendor's licence; the paper asserts CC-0 for the deposited data but the deposit itself could not be inspected in this assessment
registration required: reconstructing the journal-selection step (top-25 journals by h-index from the Journal Citation Indicator) requires authenticated access to Clarivate's platform

verification limit (not a barrier attributable to the author): supplementary and repository files were deliberately withheld from this assessment, so Tier 0 classifications rest on the paper's own explicit deposit statements rather than on retrieval
